key_insight: Coupling-Grouped XY-QAOA jointly selects anomalous samples and explanatory features under fixed budgets, reducing calibration-sensitivity and improving hardware feasibility versus sequential feature-first selection.
engineering_relevance: The method delivers shallower, lower-gate quantum circuits on IBM Heron hardware while preserving constraints, making joint constrained selection more practical for near-term quantum optimization workflows.
method: Formulate anomaly and feature selection as a joint constrained optimization problem with fixed sample and feature counts.
Use a constraint-preserving grouped-angle XY-QAOA mixer tailored to bipartite selection.
Apply hardware-aware compilation plus warm starts and near-budget repair to improve feasible solution quality.
evidence_signal: On sparse IBM Heron R3 benchmarks, the implementation cut depth by 45.9%-61.3% and two-qubit gates by 2.6%-5.2%, reached feasible-sequence retention up to 63% at 20 qubits p=5, and improved outcomes across 36-64 qubit runs.
watch_item: Performance is benchmark-dependent, and the strongest results rely on sparse instances, hardware-aware tuning, and feasible-sector retention that may not transfer directly to denser or noisier settings.
paper_title: Coupling-Grouped XY-QAOA for Joint Anomaly-Feature Selection
